## 配方筛选结果
获得文献支持的候选：candidate-1-fan-doublesalt-0.5M-NaFSI。

### 候选资料：candidate-1-fan-doublesalt-0.5M-NaFSI（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：未明确盐；总盐浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaFSI：0.5 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.5 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, PC, EMC, DEC；溶剂比例（质量）：EC=1, PC=2, EMC=6, DEC=1。
- 配方原文 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]：Ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), diethyl carbonate (DEC), methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), $NaPF_{6}$ and NaFSI used in the electrolyte are all from the commercial products of Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. and not further purified. The blank electrolyte was a mixture of 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ in EC, PC, EMC and DEC with a ratio of 1:2:6:1 (by weight). NaFSI was added to the blank electrolyte to replace part of $NaPF_{6}$ , maintaining the total content of NaFSI and $NaPF_{6}$ at 1 M. In this work, "blank" represents 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ , "0.1 M NaFSI" represents 0.1 M $NaFSI + 0.9 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.3 M NaFSI" represents 0.3 M $NaFSI + 0.7 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.5 M NaFSI" represents 0.5 M $NaFSI + 0.5 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.7 M NaFSI" represents 0.7 M $NaFSI + 0.3 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.9 M NaFSI" represents 0.9 M $NaFSI + 0.1 M NaPF_{6}$ . All electrolytes were prepared in an argon-filled glove box with $H_{2}O$ and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm.

## 候选评估
### candidate-1-fan-doublesalt-0.5M-NaFSI
评估建议：文献直接报告了与候选完全一致的 0.5 M NaFSI + 0.5 M NaPF6/EC:PC:EMC:DEC(1:2:6:1) 电解液，并在目标 NNFM111/HC 软包全电池、-20 °C、2.0-4.0 V、0.5 C 与 1 C 条件下显示低温放电容量提升；本轮无 recorded_tool_predictions 计算依据，因此推荐完全基于文献证据。
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- NaFSI/NaPF6 dual-salt electrolyte at 0.5 M NaFSI + 0.5 M NaPF6 (total 1 M)：该文将 "0.5 M NaFSI" 明确定义为 0.5 M NaFSI + 0.5 M NaPF6，且总盐浓度保持 1 M，与候选盐组成一致。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]
- 溶剂体系 EC:PC:EMC:DEC = 1:2:6:1（质量比）：基础电解液为 EC、PC、EMC、DEC 按 1:2:6:1 重量比混合，NaFSI 仅部分取代 NaPF6 而不改变溶剂配比，故候选溶剂比与原文一致。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]
- 目标体系为 NNFM111||硬碳软包全电池：原文以卷绕工艺制备 NNFM111/HC 软包全电池并给出极片配方与设计容量，与候选的目标电芯体系一致。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec4::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5::child0]
- 电压窗口 2.0-4.0 V：原文明确充放电测试在 2.0-4.0 V 电压范围进行，与目标条件匹配。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5::child0]
- -20 °C 下 0.5 C 与 1 C 放电：原文在 -20 °C 温控箱中测试 NNFM111/HC 全电池的 0.5 C 和 1 C 放电曲线，直接覆盖目标温度与倍率。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child9]
- 候选在 -20 °C 低温下具备可用放电性能：原文报告 0.5 M NaFSI 双盐体系在 -20 °C 的 0.5 C 和 1 C 放电容量分别提高 23.9% 与 26.8%，并归因于 DCR 降低，属该候选的直接低温证据。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child9]
文献与候选的关联：溶剂与盐组成段落（sec3::child0）定义 0.5 M NaFSI 双盐配方；电化学测试段落（sec5::child0）给出同一 NNFM111/HC 软包全电池在 2.0-4.0 V、-20 °C 下 0.5 C/1 C 放电的条件；性能段落（sec8::child9）报告该配方在相同全电池与温度下的容量提升，三者通过同一配方身份和同一电芯体系建立关联。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child9]
### candidate-2-fan-single-salt-1M-NaPF6
评估建议：The candidate is correctly identified as the paper's single-salt blank electrolyte, but it is the weaker branch: at -20 C at 0.5 C/1 C it delivers substantially less capacity and higher DCR than the NaFSI dual-salt system, so no evidence supports recommending it for the stated low-temperature target; the evaluation is complete but the recommendation is held.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Electrolyte identity: 1 M NaPF6 single salt in EC:PC:EMC:DEC at a 1:2:6:1 ratio by weight (the 'blank' single-salt branch).：The paper defines the blank electrolyte as 1 M NaPF6 in EC, PC, EMC and DEC at 1:2:6:1 by weight, which matches the candidate's salt, concentration, solvent set and mass-based ratio. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]
- Target system: NNFM111||hard-carbon pouch full cell.：The battery section describes wound pouch full cells with NNFM111 cathode and HC anode (design capacity 1.06 Ah), which is the same cell format named in the question. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec4::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec4]
- Operating voltage window 2.0-4.0 V.：The electrochemical measurement section states the charge/discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were run over a 2.0-4.0 V range, matching the requested window. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5]
- Low-temperature discharge capability at -20 C at 0.5 C and 1 C.：The paper reports that at -20 C the single-salt (blank) system delivers markedly less capacity than the 0.5 M NaFSI dual-salt system (0.5 C and 1 C improved by 23.9%/26.8%, higher DCR) and falls to about 0 mAh at high current density, so this candidate does not meet the low-temperature 0.5 C/1 C target. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child9][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec1::child0]
- Suitability of the single-salt branch as a selectable electrolyte (vs dual-salt) for the NNFM111/HC cell.：The single-salt system shows rapid capacity fade, fluctuating Coulombic efficiency and large impedance/gas growth versus the 0.5 M NaFSI dual-salt system, indicating it is the inferior branch rather than the recommended choice. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child5][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child7]
文献与候选的关联：The candidate's identity is the paper's 'blank' 1 M NaPF6 electrolyte, defined in the electrolyte-preparation section, and the same paper directly tests this single-salt electrolyte in wound pouch NNFM111/HC full cells over 2.0-4.0 V, including -20 C discharge at 0.5 C and 1 C and DCR, so the low-temperature comparison for this exact branch is a direct experimental association rather than an extrapolation. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child9]
### candidate-3-fan-doublesalt-0.3M-NaFSI
评估建议：候选的溶剂比例、双盐身份、电芯格式与 2.0-4.0 V 条件均有来源支持，但 -20 ℃ 0.5 C/1 C 目标速率下的性能证据在来源中仅归属 0.5 M NaFSI 双盐体系，而 0.3 M 分支被报告为约 175 圈后快速衰减，因此无法支持推荐该候选；评估已完成，故建议保留（hold）而非推荐。
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Target cell format: NNFM111||hard-carbon sodium-ion pouch full cell：来源明确制备了 NNFM111/HC 软包全电池（卷绕工艺、设计容量 1.06 Ah、N/P=1.1），与候选所面向的目标电芯一致。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec4::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec2::child1]
- Solvent composition EC:PC:EMC:DEC = 1:2:6:1 by weight：来源明确 blank 电解液为 1 M NaPF6 溶于 EC、PC、EMC、DEC（重量比 1:2:6:1），与候选溶剂比例一致。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]
- Dual-salt branch: 0.3 M NaFSI + 0.7 M NaPF6 (total 1 M)：来源定义"0.3 M NaFSI"即 0.3 M NaFSI + 0.7 M NaPF6，且总盐浓度维持 1 M，与候选配方身份相符。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]
- Charge/discharge voltage window 2.0-4.0 V：来源说明 NNFM111/HC 全电池充放电测试在 2.0-4.0 V 进行，与问题要求的电压范围一致。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5::child0]
- Target-rate discharge at -20 C: 0.5 C and 1 C for this 0.3 M NaFSI branch：来源确有 -20 ℃、0.5 C/1 C 放电测试流程，但其低温放电容量提升（0.5 C 增 23.9%、1 C 增 26.8%、DCR 降低）明确归给 0.5 M NaFSI 双盐体系，未对该 0.3 M 分支给出 -20 ℃、0.5 C/1 C 的直接数据或原文明示的可转移关系。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child9]
- Candidate branch cycling stability suitable for selection：来源指出 0.1 M 和 0.3 M NaFSI 双盐体系分别在约 100 和 175 圈后快速衰减，只有 0.5 M 稳定循环，原因是低 NaFSI 含量不足以形成稳定界面膜；这直接对该 0.3 M 候选的适用性构成反证。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child1]
文献与候选的关联：来源在 NNFM111/HC 软包全电池上注入 EC:PC:EMC:DEC=1:2:6:1（重量比）的 1 M 钠盐电解液，并在 2.0-4.0 V、-20 ℃ 以 0.5 C/1 C 放电测试；但该低温性能提升明确对应 0.5 M NaFSI 双盐分支，而 0.3 M NaFSI 分支被报告为循环快速衰减，二者配方身份不同，不能把 0.5 M 的低温结果转移到本候选。 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec4::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child9][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child1]
### candidate-4-fan-doublesalt-0.1M-NaFSI
评估建议：The composition, cell format, voltage window, and -20 °C 0.5 C/1 C protocol all match the question, so the evaluation could be completed, but the only -20 °C evidence in the sources belongs to the 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system, not the 0.1 M candidate, and the 0.1 M branch is reported to decay rapidly after ~100 cycles. With no candidate-specific low-temperature data (and no recorded computations), this candidate cannot be recommended; a held decision with the 0.5 M NaFSI branch flagged as the better-supported option is appropriate.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Electrolyte identity: NaFSI/NaPF6 dual-salt at 1 M total with 0.1 M NaFSI + 0.9 M NaPF6 in EC:PC:EMC:DEC = 1:2:6:1 by weight：The source explicitly defines the blank electrolyte as 1 M NaPF6 in EC:PC:EMC:DEC 1:2:6:1 by weight and defines "0.1 M NaFSI" as 0.1 M NaFSI + 0.9 M NaPF6 with total salt held at 1 M, matching the candidate composition and mass-ratio basis. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]
- Target system: NNFM111||hard-carbon pouch full cell：The source states the work designs the electrolyte for NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2/hard-carbon (NNFM111/HC) SIBs and describes pouch full cells prepared by winding with NNFM111 cathode and HC anode. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec2::child1][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec4::child0]
- Voltage window 2.0-4.0 V：The electrochemical measurement section states the NNFM111/HC full-cell charge/discharge tests were run at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V, matching the requested window. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5::child0]
- Low-temperature discharge at -20 °C measured at both 0.5 C and 1 C on the target full cell：The source describes discharge curves of NNFM111/HC full cells measured in a temperature-controlled chamber at -20 °C at discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C, establishing that this protocol exists for the target cell format. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5::child0]
- Candidate-specific -20 °C 0.5 C / 1 C performance for the 0.1 M NaFSI formulation：The reported -20 °C gain (0.5 C and 1 C discharge capacity increased 23.9% and 26.8%) is attributed only to the 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system, not to the 0.1 M NaFSI composition; no source gives that candidate's -20 °C result. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child9][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec1::child0]
- Low-NaFSI branch retains stable cycling relative to the better-performing branch (branch-selection relevance)：The source states cells with 0.1 M and 0.3 M NaFSI double-salt systems decayed rapidly after 100 and 175 cycles while the 0.5 M NaFSI system cycled stably, because too little NaFSI cannot form a stable film; this is room-temperature cycling and does not by itself decide the -20 °C question, but it argues against the 0.1 M branch. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child1]
文献与候选的关联：The candidate composition is anchored by the electrolyte-preparation paragraph, which defines the exact 1:2:6:1 EC:PC:EMC:DEC blank and the 0.1 M NaFSI = 0.1 M NaFSI + 0.9 M NaPF6 mapping, and by the battery/measurement paragraphs, which establish the NNFM111/HC pouch cell, 2.0-4.0 V window, and -20 °C 0.5 C/1 C protocol. However, the low-temperature capacity benefit is reported by the source only for the 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system; the link from that -20 °C result to the 0.1 M candidate is not established, so it cannot be transferred. The 0.1 M branch is instead directly associated with rapid cycling decay relative to 0.5 M NaFSI. source_refs.raw_quote: Ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), diethyl carbonate (DEC), methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), $NaPF_{6}$ and NaFSI used in the electrolyte are all from the commercial products of Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. and not further purified. The blank electrolyte was a mixture of 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ in EC, PC, EMC and DEC with a ratio of 1:2:6:1 (by weight). NaFSI was added to the blank electrolyte to replace part of $NaPF_{6}$ , maintaining the total content of NaFSI and $NaPF_{6}$ at 1 M. In this work, "blank" represents 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ , "0.1 M NaFSI" represents 0.1 M $NaFSI + 0.9 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.3 M NaFSI" represents 0.3 M $NaFSI + 0.7 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.5 M NaFSI" represents 0.5 M $NaFSI + 0.5 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.7 M NaFSI" represents 0.7 M $NaFSI + 0.3 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.9 M NaFSI" represents 0.9 M $NaFSI + 0.1 M NaPF_{6}$ . All electrolytes were prepared in an argon-filled glove box with $H_{2}O$ and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm.

source_refs.raw_quote: Sodium sheets were purchased from Guangdong Candlelight New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. NNFM111 was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and HC was from Coroli Co., Ltd. The electrolytic cell adopted a two-electrode system, with the sodium sheet as the opposite electrode and the reference electrode, and the aluminum foil and stainless steel sheet as the working electrode, respectively. The pouch full cells were prepared by winding process. cathode plate was composed of 94.6% NNFM111, 1.8% mixed adhesive (polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) binder and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR)), 1% conductive agent CNT, 0.1% maleic acid, and 2.5% Super P (SP) conductive carbon with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 3.3 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 2.8 g cm $^{-3}$ . The anode plate was composed of 95% HC, 2% mixed adhesive ((PVDF and SBR), 1.5% SP, and 1.5% maleic acid with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 16.18 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 0.9 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. To prevent the formation of Na dendrites of the decrease in Coulombic efficiency, the negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The design capacity of the battery was 1.06 Ah, and the liquid injection amount of each battery electrolyte was 5 g.

source_refs.raw_quote: Firstly, the electrolyte was injected into the pouch NNFM111/HC cells in an argon-filled glove box and then the cells were deposited at room temperature for 24 h. The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The cycle performance of NNFM111/HC full cells was measured at a constant temperature of $25^{\circ}$ C and $45^{\circ}$ C with a charge and discharge current of 1 C. The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I).

source_refs.raw_quote: Low temperature performance is also an important aspect for the application of SIBs. Figure S9 shows the discharge capability of the NNFM111/HC full cell at $-20^{\circ}C$ . It can be seen that the discharge capacity of the battery with 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system is significantly improved. Compared with the single-salt system, the discharge capacity of 0.5 C and 1 C of the batteries with 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system increased by 23.9% and 26.8%, respectively. The results of DCR test at $-20^{\circ}C$ shows (Figure S9d) that the DCR value of the battery with 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system is significantly reduced, which is the key reason why it can release more capacity at low temperatures. Especially at the high current density, the battery with 0.5 M NaFSI can maintain a discharge capacity about 200 mAh, while the discharge capacity of the battery with single-salt system is around 0 mAh.

A sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI)-based multifunctional electrolyte is developed by partially replacing $NaPF_{6}$ salt in the electrolyte to improve the wide temperature range working capability of $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}/hard$ carbon (NNFM111/HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, it is worth noting that the cells using 0.1 M and 0.3 M NaFSI double-salt system decayed rapidly after 100 and 175 cycles, while the cells with 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system cycled stably. This is because the little content of NaFSI is not enough to form a stable film on the surface of the electrode. As can be seen from Figure 4b, the battery with 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system still has a capacity retention rate of 75.5% after 250 cycles, while the corresponding value of the single-salt system is only 42.2%. In addition, the coulombic efficiency of the battery with 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system remained at about 100% during the cycle process, indicating less loss of active sodium.

The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. source_refs.raw_quote: An electrolyte containing a sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) dual-functional additive is developed to enhance the temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The addition of NaDFP in the electrolyte not only induces solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) and cathode electrolyte interphases with excellent properties on the anode and cathode surfaces but also optimizes of the solvation structure of sodium ions, resulting in a better cycle stability of NFM/HC SIBs over a wide temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . In addition, high capacity retentions of 85 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , 90 % after 150 cycles at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ and 90 % after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ are achieved, respectively. And those common problems such as gas generation and sodium evolution of pouch NFM/HC SIBs are also effectively relieved, indicating the promising application prospect of NaDFP additive in the functional electrolyte of NFM/HC SIBs.

3.2. Analysis of the electrode interfaces, solvation structure, and functionalization mechanism

source_refs.raw_quote: The sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ , 99.8% min), diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2, 99.8% min) and 2-methyloxolane (MO, 99.8% min) were purchased from DoDo Chem. Common ether electrolyte (CCE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2 solvent. Weakly solvated electrolyte (WSE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in MO solvent. Co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2: MO = 7:3 vol%. All electrolyte preparation processes were carried out in a glovebox filled with Ar (H $_2$ O < 0.1 ppm and O $_2$ < 0.1 ppm). The electrolyte salts and solvents we purchased are of anhydrous grade. After purchase, they are placed in the glove box for direct use. Hard carbon (HC) materials were purchased from Baisige New Energy Co., Ltd. The HC negative electrode was prepared by mixing the active material, CMC (CMC2200, purchased from Daicel Corporation), SBR (BM-451B, purchased from Zeon Corporation) and conductive carbon black (weight ratio 92:1.5:3.5:3) in deionized water to form a homogeneous slurry. The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . Glass fiber (GF/D, Whatman) was used as separator and metallic sodium (purchased from Canrd Technology Co. Ltd.) was used as counter electrode.

source_refs.raw_quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

source_refs.raw_quote: The Na||HC half cells with various electrolytes were assembled in Ar-filled gloveboxes using 2032-type coin cells with Na metal and HC. The amount of electrolyte was controlled at $100\mu \mathrm{L}$ for each Na||HC cell. The voltage ranges of Na||HC cells and HC||NFM pouch batteries were 0 to $2.5\mathrm{V}$ and 1.8 to $3.8\mathrm{V}$ , respectively. For pouch cells, cycle at $50\mathrm{mA}$ for $2\mathrm{h}$ , followed by $100\mathrm{mA}$ for $1\mathrm{h}$ , then $200\mathrm{mA}$ for $2.5\mathrm{h}$ . After a $36\mathrm{h}$ rest period, charge at $200\mathrm{mA}$ until full capacity is reached, then discharge to $1.8\mathrm{V}$ to complete the activation process. The entire procedure is conducted at 45 °C. The Na $^{+}$ storage performance was examined in a galvanostatic charge-discharge test on NEWARE Battery Test System (BTS-610, Shenzhen, China). The ion conductivity of the electrolyte was measured at different temperatures using the CHI660D electrochemical workstation through electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) technology. Galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT) testing was performed by NEWARE battery system. The test was performed in the third charge-discharge cycle at 20 mA g $^{-1}$ with a pulse time for 30 min and the intervals for 2 h. Acquire 1 data point every 5 seconds. LSV (scan rate: 10 mV s $^{-1}$ , voltage range: 2.5–5.5 V) tests were implemented by CHI660D electrochemical workstation.

Preparation of the Batteries
Sodium sheets were purchased from Guangdong Candlelight New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. NNFM111 was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and HC was from Coroli Co., Ltd. The electrolytic cell adopted a two-electrode system, with the sodium sheet as the opposite electrode and the reference electrode, and the aluminum foil and stainless steel sheet as the working electrode, respectively. The pouch full cells were prepared by winding process. cathode plate was composed of 94.6% NNFM111, 1.8% mixed adhesive (polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) binder and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR)), 1% conductive agent CNT, 0.1% maleic acid, and 2.5% Super P (SP) conductive carbon with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 3.3 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 2.8 g cm $^{-3}$ . The anode plate was composed of 95% HC, 2% mixed adhesive ((PVDF and SBR), 1.5% SP, and 1.5% maleic acid with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 16.18 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 0.9 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. To prevent the formation of Na dendrites of the decrease in Coulombic efficiency, the negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The design capacity of the battery was 1.06 Ah, and the liquid injection amount of each battery electrolyte was 5 g. Considering that the battery capacity is closely related to the ratio of positive and negative electrode capacities, the load of active substances, etc., universal current and capacity units (mA and mAh) instead of specific current and capacity units (mA cm $^{-2}$ or mAh g $^{-1}$ ) were used in the following discussion.

source_refs.raw_quote:
Electrochemical Measurements
Firstly, the electrolyte was injected into the pouch NNFM111/HC cells in an argon-filled glove box and then the cells were deposited at room temperature for 24 h. The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The cycle performance of NNFM111/HC full cells was measured at a constant temperature of $25^{\circ}$ C and $45^{\circ}$ C with a charge and discharge current of 1 C. The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I). The cell was first charged to 4.0 V and subsequently transferred to an explosion-proof oven (gdw-100 l, Suoyate) for constant $60^{\circ}$ C elevated temperature storage. The cyclic voltammetry (CV) and linear cyclic voltammetry scanning tests were performed on an electrochemical workstation (CHI660E, Chenhua, Shanghai). A Solartron 1470 instrument (AMETEK) was used for electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) tests, the frequency range was 100 kHz-0.01 Hz, and simultaneously apply a voltage disturbance of 10 mV.

source_refs.raw_quote: Besides the high temperature cycle, calendar aging performance at high temperature is also one of the important indicators to evaluate the cell at high temperature. Figure 6a shows the capacity retention rate and capacity recovery rate of the NNFM111/HC full cell after storing at $60^{\circ}$ C for 7 and 14 days. It can be found that the introduction of NaFSI into the single-salt system improves the battery capacity retention rate and recovery rate by 14.1%/11.6% (7D) and 4.8%/6.4% (14D), respectively. The huge improvement in calendar aging performance shows that the self-discharge of the NNFM111/HC full cell during the storage at $60^{\circ}$ C is suppressed, and the internal side reactions are reduced. By analyzing the thickness, DC resistance (DCR) and AC resistance (resistance) of the batteries after storage, it was found (Figure 6b, c) that the thickness of the battery with single-salt system change significantly during the first 7 days of storage, indicating that more gas release in the batteries. A large amount of gas fills in the battery makes the contact between the materials worse, which ultimately leads to an increase in the impedance of the battery and a drastic decrease in the capacity retention rate. At the same time, the production of a large amount of gas also means that the side reaction inside the battery is very serious, and a large amount of electrolyte components decompose to produce gas.

source_refs.raw_quote: Herein, we design a co-intercalation electrolyte (CIE) toward HC negative electrode, successfully overcoming the trade-off between $Na^{+}$ desolvation and ionic conductivity in electrolyte. Our CIE allows ions to bypass the slow desolvation process at interface and achieve sufficient diffusion in electrolyte and HC simultaneously. The free solvent regulation significantly widens the operating temperature of CIE to $-50^{\circ}C$ while ensuring sufficient solvent co-intercalation for ion storage. Meanwhile, the precisely regulated solvation structure enables appropriate participation of anions in the solvation sheath, resulting in the formation of a thinner, inorganic-rich SEI. This interphase facilitates efficient $Na^{+}$ transport across the SEI. As a result, our CIE greatly improves the low temperature performance of HC negative electrode and is further demonstrated in Ah-level SIBs cell pack. Typically, the Na ||HC cell using CIE has an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% at $25^{\circ}C$ , and an ICE of 80.5% even at the low temperature of $-50^{\circ}C$ , achieving a performance improvement compared to the existing electrolytes for HC. The CIE empowers the HC to deliver a capacity retention of 93.5% after 200 cycles at $-50^{\circ}C$ . Further assembled Ah-level HC || $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) pouch cell can achieve specific energy of $163 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $25^{\circ}C$ and $107 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $-50^{\circ}C$ .

source_refs.raw_quote: The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE. While WSE has poor rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ due to lower ionic conductivity. Figure 3b further shows the rate performance of HC at $-20^{\circ}C$ . Considering that all three electrolytes deliver similar ionic conductivity at this temperature, the variability in rate performance primarily originates from the mode of ion diffusion and interface composition. Interestingly, the rate performance of WSE is better than that of CCE at low temperature, which is attributed to the formation of a thin inorganic-rich SEI. The thicker SEI of CCE restricts the rate of $Na^{+}$ transport and even hinders solvent co-embedding, thus resulting in poor rate performance at low temperatures. In contrast, CIE with both solvent co-embedding and thin SEI show good rate performance at low temperatures. The sodium storage performance of HC at low temperature was further tested (Fig. 3c). The HC using CIE can provide a specific capacity of $269.6 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $-20^{\circ}C$ with an ICE of 91.4%, and maintains more than 80% of the ICE even at a low temperature of $-50^{\circ}C$ . Such performance is comparable to existing high-performance reports (Fig. 3d). In contrast, CCE and WSE show lower capacity and ICE at low temperatures (Fig. S15). In particular, CCE can hardly work normally at temperatures below $-30^{\circ}C$ .

citations.chunk_id: 0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec4::child0
citations.quote: Sodium sheets were purchased from Guangdong Candlelight New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. NNFM111 was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and HC was from Coroli Co., Ltd. The electrolytic cell adopted a two-electrode system, with the sodium sheet as the opposite electrode and the reference electrode, and the aluminum foil and stainless steel sheet as the working electrode, respectively. The pouch full cells were prepared by winding process. cathode plate was composed of 94.6% NNFM111, 1.8% mixed adhesive (polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) binder and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR)), 1% conductive agent CNT, 0.1% maleic acid, and 2.5% Super P (SP) conductive carbon with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 3.3 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 2.8 g cm $^{-3}$ . The anode plate was composed of 95% HC, 2% mixed adhesive ((PVDF and SBR), 1.5% SP, and 1.5% maleic acid with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 16.18 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 0.9 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. To prevent the formation of Na dendrites of the decrease in Coulombic efficiency, the negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The design capacity of the battery was 1.06 Ah, and the liquid injection amount of each battery electrolyte was 5 g.

citations.chunk_id: 0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5::child0
citations.quote: Firstly, the electrolyte was injected into the pouch NNFM111/HC cells in an argon-filled glove box and then the cells were deposited at room temperature for 24 h. The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The cycle performance of NNFM111/HC full cells was measured at a constant temperature of $25^{\circ}$ C and $45^{\circ}$ C with a charge and discharge current of 1 C. The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I).

citations.quote: Low temperature performance is also an important aspect for the application of SIBs. Figure S9 shows the discharge capability of the NNFM111/HC full cell at $-20^{\circ}C$ . It can be seen that the discharge capacity of the battery with 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system is significantly improved. Compared with the single-salt system, the discharge capacity of 0.5 C and 1 C of the batteries with 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system increased by 23.9% and 26.8%, respectively. The results of DCR test at $-20^{\circ}C$ shows (Figure S9d) that the DCR value of the battery with 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt system is significantly reduced, which is the key reason why it can release more capacity at low temperatures. The rate capability of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}C$ is displayed in Figure S10, the rate capability of the battery with 0.5 M NaFSI is slightly higher than that of the battery with single-salt system. Especially at the high current density, the battery with 0.5 M NaFSI can maintain a discharge capacity about 200 mAh, while the discharge capacity of the battery with single-salt system is around 0 mAh.

citations.quote: Besides the high temperature cycle, calendar aging performance at high temperature is also one of the important indicators to evaluate the cell at high temperature. Figure 6a shows the capacity retention rate and capacity recovery rate of the NNFM111/HC full cell after storing at $60^{\circ}$ C for 7 and 14 days. It can be found that the introduction of NaFSI into the single-salt system improves the battery capacity retention rate and recovery rate by 14.1%/11.6% (7D) and 4.8%/6.4% (14D), respectively. By analyzing the thickness, DC resistance (DCR) and AC resistance (resistance) of the batteries after storage, it was found (Figure 6b, c) that the thickness of the battery with single-salt system change significantly during the first 7 days of storage, indicating that more gas release in the batteries. A large amount of gas fills in the battery makes the contact between the materials worse, which ultimately leads to an increase in the impedance of the battery and a drastic decrease in the capacity retention rate. At the same time, the production of a large amount of gas also means that the side reaction inside the battery is very serious, and a large amount of electrolyte components decompose to produce gas.

citations.quote: An electrolyte containing a sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) dual-functional additive is developed to enhance the temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The addition of NaDFP in the electrolyte not only induces solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) and cathode electrolyte interphases with excellent properties on the anode and cathode surfaces but also optimizes of the solvation structure of sodium ions, resulting in a better cycle stability of NFM/HC SIBs over a wide temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . In addition, high capacity retentions of 85 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , 90 % after 150 cycles at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ and 90 % after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ are achieved, respectively. And those common problems such as gas generation and sodium evolution of pouch NFM/HC SIBs are also effectively relieved, indicating the promising application prospect of NaDFP additive in the functional electrolyte of NFM/HC SIBs.

Common ether electrolyte (CCE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2 solvent. Weakly solvated electrolyte (WSE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in MO solvent. Co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2: MO = 7:3 vol%. All electrolyte preparation processes were carried out in a glovebox filled with Ar (H $_2$ O < 0.1 ppm and O $_2$ < 0.1 ppm). The electrolyte salts and solvents we purchased are of anhydrous grade. After purchase, they are placed in the glove box for direct use. Hard carbon (HC) materials were purchased from Baisige New Energy Co., Ltd. The HC negative electrode was prepared by mixing the active material, CMC (CMC2200, purchased from Daicel Corporation), SBR (BM-451B, purchased from Zeon Corporation) and conductive carbon black (weight ratio 92:1.5:3.5:3) in deionized water to form a homogeneous slurry. The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

citations.chunk_id: 0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec1::child3
citations.quote: Herein, we design a co-intercalation electrolyte (CIE) toward HC negative electrode, successfully overcoming the trade-off between $Na^{+}$ desolvation and ionic conductivity in electrolyte. Our CIE allows ions to bypass the slow desolvation process at interface and achieve sufficient diffusion in electrolyte and HC simultaneously. The free solvent regulation significantly widens the operating temperature of CIE to $-50^{\circ}C$ while ensuring sufficient solvent co-intercalation for ion storage. Meanwhile, the precisely regulated solvation structure enables appropriate participation of anions in the solvation sheath, resulting in the formation of a thinner, inorganic-rich SEI. This interphase facilitates efficient $Na^{+}$ transport across the SEI. As a result, our CIE greatly improves the low temperature performance of HC negative electrode and is further demonstrated in Ah-level SIBs cell pack. Typically, the Na ||HC cell using CIE has an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% at $25^{\circ}C$ , and an ICE of 80.5% even at the low temperature of $-50^{\circ}C$ , achieving a performance improvement compared to the existing electrolytes for HC. The CIE empowers the HC to deliver a capacity retention of 93.5% after 200 cycles at $-50^{\circ}C$ . Further assembled Ah-level HC || $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) pouch cell can achieve specific energy of $163 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $25^{\circ}C$ and $107 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $-50^{\circ}C$ .

citations.quote: The Na||HC half cells with various electrolytes were assembled in Ar-filled gloveboxes using 2032-type coin cells with Na metal and HC. The amount of electrolyte was controlled at $100\mu \mathrm{L}$ for each Na||HC cell. The voltage ranges of Na||HC cells and HC||NFM pouch batteries were 0 to $2.5\mathrm{V}$ and 1.8 to $3.8\mathrm{V}$ , respectively. For pouch cells, cycle at $50\mathrm{mA}$ for $2\mathrm{h}$ , followed by $100\mathrm{mA}$ for $1\mathrm{h}$ , then $200\mathrm{mA}$ for $2.5\mathrm{h}$ . After a $36\mathrm{h}$ rest period, charge at $200\mathrm{mA}$ until full capacity is reached, then discharge to $1.8\mathrm{V}$ to complete the activation process. The entire procedure is conducted at 45 °C. The Na $^{+}$ storage performance was examined in a galvanostatic charge-discharge test on NEWARE Battery Test System (BTS-610, Shenzhen, China). The ion conductivity of the electrolyte was measured at different temperatures using the CHI660D electrochemical workstation through electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) technology. Galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT) testing was performed by NEWARE battery system. The test was performed in the third charge-discharge cycle at 20 mA g $^{-1}$ with a pulse time for 30 min and the intervals for 2 h. Acquire 1 data point every 5 seconds. LSV (scan rate: 10 mV s $^{-1}$ , voltage range: 2.5–5.5 V) tests were implemented by CHI660D electrochemical workstation.

citations.quote: The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE. While WSE has poor rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ due to lower ionic conductivity. Figure 3b further shows the rate performance of HC at $-20^{\circ}C$ . Considering that all three electrolytes deliver similar ionic conductivity at this temperature, the variability in rate performance primarily originates from the mode of ion diffusion and interface composition. Interestingly, the rate performance of WSE is better than that of CCE at low temperature, which is attributed to the formation of a thin inorganic-rich SEI. The thicker SEI of CCE restricts the rate of $Na^{+}$ transport and even hinders solvent co-embedding, thus resulting in poor rate performance at low temperatures. In contrast, CIE with both solvent co-embedding and thin SEI show good rate performance at low temperatures. The sodium storage performance of HC at low temperature was further tested (Fig. 3c). The HC using CIE can provide a specific capacity of $269.6 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $-20^{\circ}C$ with an ICE of 91.4%, and maintains more than 80% of the ICE even at a low temperature of $-50^{\circ}C$ . citations.quote: The Na||HC half cells with various electrolytes were assembled in Ar-filled gloveboxes using 2032-type coin cells with Na metal and HC. The amount of electrolyte was controlled at $100\mu \mathrm{L}$ for each Na||HC cell. The voltage ranges of Na||HC cells and HC||NFM pouch batteries were 0 to $2.5\mathrm{V}$ and 1.8 to $3.8\mathrm{V}$ , respectively. For pouch cells, cycle at $50\mathrm{mA}$ for $2\mathrm{h}$ , followed by $100\mathrm{mA}$ for $1\mathrm{h}$ , then $200\mathrm{mA}$ for $2.5\mathrm{h}$ . After a $36\mathrm{h}$ rest period, charge at $200\mathrm{mA}$ until full capacity is reached, then discharge to $1.8\mathrm{V}$ to complete the activation process. The entire procedure is conducted at 45 °C. The Na $^{+}$ storage performance was examined in a galvanostatic charge-discharge test on NEWARE Battery Test System (BTS-610, Shenzhen, China). The ion conductivity of the electrolyte was measured at different temperatures using the CHI660D electrochemical workstation through electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) technology. Galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT) testing was performed by NEWARE battery system. The test was performed in the third charge-discharge cycle at 20 mA g $^{-1}$ with a pulse time for 30 min and the intervals for 2 h. Acquire 1 data point every 5 seconds. LSV (scan rate: 10 mV s $^{-1}$ , voltage range: 2.5–5.5 V) tests were implemented by CHI660D electrochemical workstation.

association_citations.quote: The sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ , 99.8% min), diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2, 99.8% min) and 2-methyloxolane (MO, 99.8% min) were purchased from DoDo Chem. Common ether electrolyte (CCE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2 solvent. Weakly solvated electrolyte (WSE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in MO solvent. Co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2: MO = 7:3 vol%. All electrolyte preparation processes were carried out in a glovebox filled with Ar (H $_2$ O < 0.1 ppm and O $_2$ < 0.1 ppm). The electrolyte salts and solvents we purchased are of anhydrous grade. After purchase, they are placed in the glove box for direct use. Hard carbon (HC) materials were purchased from Baisige New Energy Co., Ltd. The HC negative electrode was prepared by mixing the active material, CMC (CMC2200, purchased from Daicel Corporation), SBR (BM-451B, purchased from Zeon Corporation) and conductive carbon black (weight ratio 92:1.5:3.5:3) in deionized water to form a homogeneous slurry. The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . Glass fiber (GF/D, Whatman) was used as separator and metallic sodium (purchased from Canrd Technology Co. Ltd.) was used as counter electrode.

association_citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

The electrolytic cell adopted a two-electrode system, with the sodium sheet as the opposite electrode and the reference electrode, and the aluminum foil and stainless steel sheet as the working electrode, respectively. The pouch full cells were prepared by winding process. cathode plate was composed of 94.6% NNFM111, 1.8% mixed adhesive (polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) binder and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR)), 1% conductive agent CNT, 0.1% maleic acid, and 2.5% Super P (SP) conductive carbon with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 3.3 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 2.8 g cm $^{-3}$ . The anode plate was composed of 95% HC, 2% mixed adhesive ((PVDF and SBR), 1.5% SP, and 1.5% maleic acid with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 16.18 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 0.9 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. To prevent the formation of Na dendrites of the decrease in Coulombic efficiency, the negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The design capacity of the battery was 1.06 Ah, and the liquid injection amount of each battery electrolyte was 5 g.

evidence_ledger.quote: Firstly, the electrolyte was injected into the pouch NNFM111/HC cells in an argon-filled glove box and then the cells were deposited at room temperature for 24 h. The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The cycle performance of NNFM111/HC full cells was measured at a constant temperature of $25^{\circ}$ C and $45^{\circ}$ C with a charge and discharge current of 1 C. The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I).

Electrochemical Measurements
Firstly, the electrolyte was injected into the pouch NNFM111/HC cells in an argon-filled glove box and then the cells were deposited at room temperature for 24 h. The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The cycle performance of NNFM111/HC full cells was measured at a constant temperature of $25^{\circ}$ C and $45^{\circ}$ C with a charge and discharge current of 1 C. The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I). The cell was first charged to 4.0 V and subsequently transferred to an explosion-proof oven (gdw-100 l, Suoyate) for constant $60^{\circ}$ C elevated temperature storage. The cyclic voltammetry (CV) and linear cyclic voltammetry scanning tests were performed on an electrochemical workstation (CHI660E, Chenhua, Shanghai). A Solartron 1470 instrument (AMETEK) was used for electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) tests, the frequency range was 100 kHz-0.01 Hz, and simultaneously apply a voltage disturbance of 10 mV.

evidence_ledger.quote: Herein, we design a co-intercalation electrolyte (CIE) toward HC negative electrode, successfully overcoming the trade-off between $Na^{+}$ desolvation and ionic conductivity in electrolyte. Our CIE allows ions to bypass the slow desolvation process at interface and achieve sufficient diffusion in electrolyte and HC simultaneously. The free solvent regulation significantly widens the operating temperature of CIE to $-50^{\circ}C$ while ensuring sufficient solvent co-intercalation for ion storage. Meanwhile, the precisely regulated solvation structure enables appropriate participation of anions in the solvation sheath, resulting in the formation of a thinner, inorganic-rich SEI. This interphase facilitates efficient $Na^{+}$ transport across the SEI. As a result, our CIE greatly improves the low temperature performance of HC negative electrode and is further demonstrated in Ah-level SIBs cell pack. Typically, the Na ||HC cell using CIE has an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% at $25^{\circ}C$ , and an ICE of 80.5% even at the low temperature of $-50^{\circ}C$ , achieving a performance improvement compared to the existing electrolytes for HC. The CIE empowers the HC to deliver a capacity retention of 93.5% after 200 cycles at $-50^{\circ}C$ . Further assembled Ah-level HC || $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) pouch cell can achieve specific energy of $163 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $25^{\circ}C$ and $107 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $-50^{\circ}C$ .

NNFM111 was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and HC was from Coroli Co., Ltd. The electrolytic cell adopted a two-electrode system, with the sodium sheet as the opposite electrode and the reference electrode, and the aluminum foil and stainless steel sheet as the working electrode, respectively. The pouch full cells were prepared by winding process. cathode plate was composed of 94.6% NNFM111, 1.8% mixed adhesive (polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) binder and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR)), 1% conductive agent CNT, 0.1% maleic acid, and 2.5% Super P (SP) conductive carbon with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 3.3 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 2.8 g cm $^{-3}$ . The anode plate was composed of 95% HC, 2% mixed adhesive ((PVDF and SBR), 1.5% SP, and 1.5% maleic acid with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 16.18 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 0.9 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. To prevent the formation of Na dendrites of the decrease in Coulombic efficiency, the negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The design capacity of the battery was 1.06 Ah, and the liquid injection amount of each battery electrolyte was 5 g.

citations.quote: Firstly, the electrolyte was injected into the pouch NNFM111/HC cells in an argon-filled glove box and then the cells were deposited at room temperature for 24 h. The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The cycle performance of NNFM111/HC full cells was measured at a constant temperature of $25^{\circ}$ C and $45^{\circ}$ C with a charge and discharge current of 1 C. The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I).

Preparation of the Batteries
Sodium sheets were purchased from Guangdong Candlelight New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. NNFM111 was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and HC was from Coroli Co., Ltd. The electrolytic cell adopted a two-electrode system, with the sodium sheet as the opposite electrode and the reference electrode, and the aluminum foil and stainless steel sheet as the working electrode, respectively. The pouch full cells were prepared by winding process. cathode plate was composed of 94.6% NNFM111, 1.8% mixed adhesive (polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) binder and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR)), 1% conductive agent CNT, 0.1% maleic acid, and 2.5% Super P (SP) conductive carbon with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 3.3 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 2.8 g cm $^{-3}$ . The anode plate was composed of 95% HC, 2% mixed adhesive ((PVDF and SBR), 1.5% SP, and 1.5% maleic acid with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 16.18 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 0.9 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. To prevent the formation of Na dendrites of the decrease in Coulombic efficiency, the negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The design capacity of the battery was 1.06 Ah, and the liquid injection amount of each battery electrolyte was 5 g. Considering that the battery capacity is closely related to the ratio of positive and negative electrode capacities, the load of active substances, etc., universal current and capacity units (mA and mAh) instead of specific current and capacity units (mA cm $^{-2}$ or mAh g $^{-1}$ ) were used in the following discussion.

Electrochemical Measurements
Firstly, the electrolyte was injected into the pouch NNFM111/HC cells in an argon-filled glove box and then the cells were deposited at room temperature for 24 h. The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The cycle performance of NNFM111/HC full cells was measured at a constant temperature of $25^{\circ}$ C and $45^{\circ}$ C with a charge and discharge current of 1 C. The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I). The cell was first charged to 4.0 V and subsequently transferred to an explosion-proof oven (gdw-100 l, Suoyate) for constant $60^{\circ}$ C elevated temperature storage. The cyclic voltammetry (CV) and linear cyclic voltammetry scanning tests were performed on an electrochemical workstation (CHI660E, Chenhua, Shanghai). A Solartron 1470 instrument (AMETEK) was used for electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) tests, the frequency range was 100 kHz-0.01 Hz, and simultaneously apply a voltage disturbance of 10 mV.

citations.quote: Besides the high temperature cycle, calendar aging performance at high temperature is also one of the important indicators to evaluate the cell at high temperature. Figure 6a shows the capacity retention rate and capacity recovery rate of the NNFM111/HC full cell after storing at $60^{\circ}$ C for 7 and 14 days. It can be found that the introduction of NaFSI into the single-salt system improves the battery capacity retention rate and recovery rate by 14.1%/11.6% (7D) and 4.8%/6.4% (14D), respectively. The huge improvement in calendar aging performance shows that the self-discharge of the NNFM111/HC full cell during the storage at $60^{\circ}$ C is suppressed, and the internal side reactions are reduced. By analyzing the thickness, DC resistance (DCR) and AC resistance (resistance) of the batteries after storage, it was found (Figure 6b, c) that the thickness of the battery with single-salt system change significantly during the first 7 days of storage, indicating that more gas release in the batteries. A large amount of gas fills in the battery makes the contact between the materials worse, which ultimately leads to an increase in the impedance of the battery and a drastic decrease in the capacity retention rate. At the same time, the production of a large amount of gas also means that the side reaction inside the battery is very serious, and a large amount of electrolyte components decompose to produce gas.

The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I).

A sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI)-based multifunctional electrolyte is developed by partially replacing $NaPF_{6}$ salt in the electrolyte to improve the wide temperature range working capability of $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}/hard$ carbon (NNFM111/HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The capacity retention of the SIBs with NaFSI- $NaPF_{6}$ dual salt electrolyte increases from 47.2% to 75.5% after 250 cycles at 25°C, and from 51.0% to 82.3% after 80 cycles at 45°C, and the 1 C discharge capacity retention at the low temperature of -20°C also increases 26.8%. association_citations.quote: Ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), diethyl carbonate (DEC), methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), $NaPF_{6}$ and NaFSI used in the electrolyte are all from the commercial products of Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. and not further purified. association_citations.chunk_id: 0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec4::child0
association_citations.quote: Sodium sheets were purchased from Guangdong Candlelight New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. NNFM111 was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and HC was from Coroli Co., Ltd. The electrolytic cell adopted a two-electrode system, with the sodium sheet as the opposite electrode and the reference electrode, and the aluminum foil and stainless steel sheet as the working electrode, respectively. The pouch full cells were prepared by winding process. cathode plate was composed of 94.6% NNFM111, 1.8% mixed adhesive (polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) binder and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR)), 1% conductive agent CNT, 0.1% maleic acid, and 2.5% Super P (SP) conductive carbon with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 3.3 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 2.8 g cm $^{-3}$ . The anode plate was composed of 95% HC, 2% mixed adhesive ((PVDF and SBR), 1.5% SP, and 1.5% maleic acid with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 16.18 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 0.9 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. To prevent the formation of Na dendrites of the decrease in Coulombic efficiency, the negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The design capacity of the battery was 1.06 Ah, and the liquid injection amount of each battery electrolyte was 5 g.

association_citations.chunk_id: 0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5::child0
association_citations.quote: Firstly, the electrolyte was injected into the pouch NNFM111/HC cells in an argon-filled glove box and then the cells were deposited at room temperature for 24 h. The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The cycle performance of NNFM111/HC full cells was measured at a constant temperature of $25^{\circ}$ C and $45^{\circ}$ C with a charge and discharge current of 1 C. The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I).

citations.chunk_id: 0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec2::child0
citations.quote: An electrolyte containing a sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) dual-functional additive is developed to enhance the temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The addition of NaDFP in the electrolyte not only induces solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) and cathode electrolyte interphases with excellent properties on the anode and cathode surfaces but also optimizes of the solvation structure of sodium ions, resulting in a better cycle stability of NFM/HC SIBs over a wide temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . In addition, high capacity retentions of 85 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , 90 % after 150 cycles at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ and 90 % after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ are achieved, respectively. And those common problems such as gas generation and sodium evolution of pouch NFM/HC SIBs are also effectively relieved, indicating the promising application prospect of NaDFP additive in the functional electrolyte of NFM/HC SIBs.

citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

citations.quote: Herein, we design a co-intercalation electrolyte (CIE) toward HC negative electrode, successfully overcoming the trade-off between $Na^{+}$ desolvation and ionic conductivity in electrolyte. Our CIE allows ions to bypass the slow desolvation process at interface and achieve sufficient diffusion in electrolyte and HC simultaneously. The free solvent regulation significantly widens the operating temperature of CIE to $-50^{\circ}C$ while ensuring sufficient solvent co-intercalation for ion storage. Meanwhile, the precisely regulated solvation structure enables appropriate participation of anions in the solvation sheath, resulting in the formation of a thinner, inorganic-rich SEI. This interphase facilitates efficient $Na^{+}$ transport across the SEI. As a result, our CIE greatly improves the low temperature performance of HC negative electrode and is further demonstrated in Ah-level SIBs cell pack. Typically, the Na ||HC cell using CIE has an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% at $25^{\circ}C$ , and an ICE of 80.5% even at the low temperature of $-50^{\circ}C$ , achieving a performance improvement compared to the existing electrolytes for HC. The CIE empowers the HC to deliver a capacity retention of 93.5% after 200 cycles at $-50^{\circ}C$ . Further assembled Ah-level HC || $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) pouch cell can achieve specific energy of $163 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $25^{\circ}C$ and $107 Wh kg^{-1}$ at $-50^{\circ}C$ .

citations.quote: The Na||HC half cells with various electrolytes were assembled in Ar-filled gloveboxes using 2032-type coin cells with Na metal and HC. The amount of electrolyte was controlled at $100\mu \mathrm{L}$ for each Na||HC cell. The voltage ranges of Na||HC cells and HC||NFM pouch batteries were 0 to $2.5\mathrm{V}$ and 1.8 to $3.8\mathrm{V}$ , respectively. For pouch cells, cycle at $50\mathrm{mA}$ for $2\mathrm{h}$ , followed by $100\mathrm{mA}$ for $1\mathrm{h}$ , then $200\mathrm{mA}$ for $2.5\mathrm{h}$ . After a $36\mathrm{h}$ rest period, charge at $200\mathrm{mA}$ until full capacity is reached, then discharge to $1.8\mathrm{V}$ to complete the activation process. The entire procedure is conducted at 45 °C. The Na $^{+}$ storage performance was examined in a galvanostatic charge-discharge test on NEWARE Battery Test System (BTS-610, Shenzhen, China). The ion conductivity of the electrolyte was measured at different temperatures using the CHI660D electrochemical workstation through electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) technology. Galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT) testing was performed by NEWARE battery system. The test was performed in the third charge-discharge cycle at 20 mA g $^{-1}$ with a pulse time for 30 min and the intervals for 2 h. Acquire 1 data point every 5 seconds. LSV (scan rate: 10 mV s $^{-1}$ , voltage range: 2.5–5.5 V) tests were implemented by CHI660D electrochemical workstation.

citations.quote: The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE. While WSE has poor rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ due to lower ionic conductivity. Figure 3b further shows the rate performance of HC at $-20^{\circ}C$ . Considering that all three electrolytes deliver similar ionic conductivity at this temperature, the variability in rate performance primarily originates from the mode of ion diffusion and interface composition. Interestingly, the rate performance of WSE is better than that of CCE at low temperature, which is attributed to the formation of a thin inorganic-rich SEI. The thicker SEI of CCE restricts the rate of $Na^{+}$ transport and even hinders solvent co-embedding, thus resulting in poor rate performance at low temperatures. In contrast, CIE with both solvent co-embedding and thin SEI show good rate performance at low temperatures. The sodium storage performance of HC at low temperature was further tested (Fig. 3c). The HC using CIE can provide a specific capacity of $269.6 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $-20^{\circ}C$ with an ICE of 91.4%, and maintains more than 80% of the ICE even at a low temperature of $-50^{\circ}C$ . Such performance is comparable to existing high-performance reports (Fig. 3d). In contrast, CCE and WSE show lower capacity and ICE at low temperatures (Fig. S15). In particular, CCE can hardly work normally at temperatures below $-30^{\circ}C$ .

Preparation of the Batteries
Sodium sheets were purchased from Guangdong Candlelight New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. NNFM111 was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and HC was from Coroli Co., Ltd. The electrolytic cell adopted a two-electrode system, with the sodium sheet as the opposite electrode and the reference electrode, and the aluminum foil and stainless steel sheet as the working electrode, respectively. The pouch full cells were prepared by winding process. cathode plate was composed of 94.6% NNFM111, 1.8% mixed adhesive (polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) binder and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR)), 1% conductive agent CNT, 0.1% maleic acid, and 2.5% Super P (SP) conductive carbon with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 3.3 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 2.8 g cm $^{-3}$ . The anode plate was composed of 95% HC, 2% mixed adhesive ((PVDF and SBR), 1.5% SP, and 1.5% maleic acid with an aluminum substrate as the current collector. The area density and compaction density were 16.18 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 0.9 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. To prevent the formation of Na dendrites of the decrease in Coulombic efficiency, the negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The design capacity of the battery was 1.06 Ah, and the liquid injection amount of each battery electrolyte was 5 g. Considering that the battery capacity is closely related to the ratio of positive and negative electrode capacities, the load of active substances, etc., universal current and capacity units (mA and mAh) instead of specific current and capacity units (mA cm $^{-2}$ or mAh g $^{-1}$ ) were used in the following discussion.
